title: Austria: Austrian-based authorised representative for foreign sellers
summary: Since 1 January 2023 a company without an Austrian establishment that sells packaging or packaged goods directly to a private end consumer in Austria via distance selling must appoint an Austrian-based authorised representative to hold its packaging obligations. A seller who only sells to businesses (B2B) has an optional right to appoint one, not a duty.

required_evidence.label: Signed appointment of the authorised representative

sources.title: § 16a-16d Verpackungsverordnung (ARA — Bevollmächtigter Vertreter)
sources.note: Fetched the regulation text directly. § 12b(1) AWG 2002 makes appointment MANDATORY ('haben ... zu bestellen') only for the Primaerverpflichtete defined at § 13g(1)(5) -- 'Versandhaendler, die keinen Sitz und keine Niederlassung in Oesterreich haben und die Verpackungen ... in Oesterreich an einen PRIVATEN Letztverbraucher im Rahmen des Fernabsatzes uebergeben' (distance sellers with no AT seat selling to PRIVATE end consumers). Separately, § 16a VerpackVO gives EU-established sellers who sell to NON-private (business) end users only an OPTIONAL right to appoint one ('koennen') -- not a duty. Confirmed the effective date precisely: § 16a(5), appointment can be made from 1 Oct. 2022 but 'entfaltet ... erst mit 1. Jaenner 2023 Rechtswirkung' (has legal effect only from 1 Jan 2023) -- matches effective_from exactly. DECISION (Tabeen Raoof, 2026-09-20, PR #6 review): held at first review of this pass, same shape as D-040 -- 'Rescope this to apply strictly to B2C distance sales (private end-consumers) so commercial B2B shipments aren't falsely flagged.' RESOLVED by adding organisation.sells_direct_to_end_users: true to applies_when, reusing the exact fact introduced for eu.ppwr.authorised-representative (D-040) rather than inventing a new one -- same underlying B2C/B2B distinction, same fix shape.
